editorContent.section: Facing cancer while growing a family
editorContent.value: Amy Jensen was hoping for another baby when persistent changes in her breast led her to seek further testing. On the morning of a planned biopsy, she learned she was pregnant. She later pursued the biopsy at around thirteen weeks of pregnancy and was diagnosed with HER2-positive invasive ductal carcinoma.

editorContent.label: Paragraph
editorContent.section: Facing cancer while growing a family
editorContent.value: Amy and her husband, Chad, shared the news with their daughters. Alongside concerns about treatment, Amy worried about how losing her hair might affect her children.

editorContent.label: Paragraph
editorContent.section: Facing cancer while growing a family
editorContent.value: At eighteen weeks pregnant, Amy underwent surgery with Dr. Teresa Reading at IMC Hospital, including a mastectomy and reconstruction. Her subsequent care at Utah Cancer Specialists included chemotherapy and Herceptin.

editorContent.value: The July 2019 account reported that Amy was cancer-free. Her family had also welcomed Jacob, born in December 2018.
